9b386223cd.brief: This NCCS notification (F. No. NCCS/SC/3-1/2025-26-Part(2), dated 13.08.2026) continues the earlier notification (NCCS/SC/3-1/2025-26-Part(2) dated 30.03.2026) and states in paragraph 1 that the earlier grant of exemption "for cloud-based IP Routers and Wi-Fi CPEs till 31st August, 2026" is continued, and in paragraph 2 that "the grant of exemption from security certification to such products is hereby extended till 31st December, 2026." The notification is issued "with the approval of Sr. DDG, NCCS," signed by ADG (Security Certification-I), and is addressed to "All OEMs/Dealers/Importers/applicants/TSTLs — through NCCS website" (copy list at end, and a request to eTT and C-DOT to make portal changes).
9b386223cd.so_what: Per the notification's operative text, the exemption from security certification for cloud-based IP Routers and Wi‑Fi CPEs granted earlier is extended until 31st December, 2026.

d90090c2ea.brief: This TRAI Direction dated August 10, 2026 directs that the 1601 numbering series, allocated by DoT (DoT letter dated 30.06.2026), be implemented in a phased manner for Service and Transactional Voice Calls by entities in sectors other than BFSI and Government (paragraphs 1–3). During Phase‑I, "Access Providers shall allocate numbering resources from the 1601 numbering series only to the eligible entities belonging to the sectors specified in Annexure‑I" (paragraph 4); Annexure‑I lists two sectors: Utilities ("Electricity distribution companies, water utilities, city gas distribution companies, LPG distribution entities, and such other utility service providers") and Logistics and courier services (illustrative principal entities listed). Access Providers must "complete onboarding and migration of all eligible Principal Entities covered under Phase‑I within ninety (90) days from the date of issue of this letter" (paragraph 5) and, when assigning numbers, comply with the DoT conditions, "verify the eligibility of the entity," "obtain an undertaking... regarding exclusive use of the numbering resources for Service and Transactional Voice Calls," assign numbers "only as ten‑digit numbers," and "comply with all applicable provisions of the TCCCPR, 2018, and directions issued by the Authority" (paragraph 6(i)–(v)). The Direction requires exclusive use of 1601 numbers for Service and Transactional Voice Calls and states: "Under no circumstances shall such numbering resources be used for Promotional Voice Calls" (paragraph 7); it also mandates publicity (paragraph 8), ten‑day status reports to TRAI during the 90‑day period including number allotted, name and sector, and migration status (paragraph 9), and a final compliance report within fifteen days after expiry of the ninety‑day period (paragraph 10). The Direction "shall come into force with immediate effect" (paragraph 11).
d90090c2ea.so_what: For Phase‑I (effective immediately from the letter dated August 10, 2026), an Access Provider must allocate 1601 series numbers only to entities in Annexure‑I, complete onboarding/migration within ninety (90) days, comply with paragraph 6(i)–(v) (including obtaining the DoT‑prescribed undertaking and assigning only ten‑digit numbers), submit status reports every ten (10) days, and a final compliance report within fifteen days after the 90‑day period.

d1351b3d6d.brief: This Consultation Paper (dated 5th August 2026) publishes a draft notification titled "The Standards of Quality of Service of Access (Wireline and Wireless) and Broadband (Wireline and Wireless) Service (First Amendment) Regulations, 2026" that, if made, will come into force "with effect from 1st October 2026" (Reg.1). It inserts a definition of "Physical Resource Block"/"PRB" into regulation 2(1) as clause (sa); renames the parameter in regulation 4(1)(ii) to "Fault incidences (No. of faults per 100 subscribers/month)"; and amends multiple QoS benchmarks in regulation 6(1) (e.g. (i) "Accuracy of service wise geospatial coverage map published on service provider’s website ≥ 98% Monthly 01.10.2026", (iv) "Percentage of significant network outage reported to the Authority within 24 hrs... 100% Monthly 01.10.2026", (xiv) "Tariff offerings in which 80th percentile value... ≥ offered typical download and upload speed for 4G/5G technology 100% Monthly 01.10.2026") and inserts a new network-slicing parameter (6(1)(xv)) "Cells having daily PRB utilisation > 80% (in 5G network) ≤ 1% Monthly 01.10.2026". The draft also inserts regulation 6(3) requiring that "Every service provider, planning to create a new network slice in their 5G network, shall submit the details of proposed and existing network slice parameters, at least twenty one (21) days in advance to the Authority... in such manner and format as may be directed by the Authority"; adds Silence Call Rate ≤ 1% in regulation 7(1)(vii) (Monthly, effective 01.10.2026); amends regulation 9 to change some benchmarks (e.g. tariff offerings to 90th percentile 100% Quarterly, Fault incidences ≤ 5 Quarterly), adds Mean Time-To-Repair (MTTR) ≤ 10 hours (Quarterly) and a broadband-equivalent definition of "Significant Network Outage" with identical rebate provisions for outages > 24 hrs; changes regulation 10 to require "Resolution of billing/charging complaints within one week 100%" and deletes the proviso on aggregated benchmarks for providers offering both access (wireline) and broadband (wireline); inserts a new QoES item in regulation 15(1)(e); amends regulation 16(1) to add the words "per compliance report"; deletes old sub‑regs (2)–(4) of regulation 16; and inserts new regulation 16A which provides that if a compliance report under regulation 13 "is found to be false, it shall... be liable to pay an amount, by way of financial disincentive, not exceeding rupees two lakhs per benchmark per compliance report" for the first contravention, and "if... false for the same parameter consecutively in two or more months or quarters... liable... not exceeding rupees five lakhs for the second consecutive false reporting and not exceeding rupees ten lakhs for each consecutive false reporting occurring thereafter."
d1351b3d6d.so_what: Per the draft, service providers will be required, effective 1st October 2026, to meet the revised numeric benchmarks (e.g. ≥98% coverage-map accuracy; Cells with daily PRB utilisation >80% ≤1%), to pre-notify new 5G network slices at least twenty one (21) days to the Authority (Reg.6(3)), and will be subject to the new financial-disincentive regime in Reg.16A (up to Rs.2 lakh per benchmark per compliance report for first contravention, escalating to Rs.5 lakh and Rs.10 lakh for repeat contraventions).

1fd813a8c1.brief: This is a corrigendum (S.O. 3348(E)) dated 23 June 2026 to the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting notification S.O. 3011(E) dated 11 June 2026 issued under "clause (s) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Sports Broadcasting Signals (Mandatory Sharing with Prasar Bharati) Act, 2007" read with "sub-rule (1) of rule 6" of the Rules, 2007. The corrigendum states that in the English version of S.O. 3011(E), at page 3, lines 24-25, the phrase "(a) All official One -Day, Twenty -20 and Test matches played by the Indian Men’s and Women’s Cricket World Cup Team and all International Cricket Council Test matches  featuring India;" shall be read as "(a) All official One-Day, Twenty-20 and Test matches played by the Indian Men’s and Women’s Cricket Team and all International Cricket Council Test matches featuring India;". S.O. 3011(E) (dated 11 June 2026) is the notification that "hereby notifies following events as sporting events of national importance" and contains the list of events (including item A.(a) for cricket) that the corrigendum amends in the English text.
1fd813a8c1.so_what: The corrigendum (S.O. 3348(E), dated 23 June 2026) directs that the English text of S.O. 3011(E) dated 11 June 2026 be read with the specified replacement: paragraph A.(a) now reads "All official One-Day, Twenty-20 and Test matches played by the Indian Men’s and Women’s Cricket Team and all International Cricket Council Test matches featuring India;".

0660fc344a.brief: Notification No. J-11013/35/2024-DM dated 22.06.2026 (Ministry of Information & Broadcasting) invokes the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi Order dated 19.06.2026 in W.P.(C) No. 8284/2026 and directs intermediaries to “take down, remove, block, disable, de-index and restrict access” to “fake and fabricated news, articles, videos and related material” featuring or purporting to depict the alleged participation, association or involvement of the Hon'ble Chief Justice of India, Hon'ble Judges of the Supreme Court of India and the High Courts, and Hon'ble Union Ministers in the 2nd International Bar & Bench Badminton Championship held in London on 07.06.2026, “together with any identical, mirrored, modified, edited, clipped, reproduced, re-uploaded, derivative or substantially similar versions thereof” within “24 hours of receipt of this Notification.” The Notification cites section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, rule 3(1)(d) and rule 7 of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, and states that “Part II of the IT Rules, 2021 … apply to publishers of news and current affairs content and publishers of online curated content on digital media” administered by MIB. It further directs intermediaries to “preserve and furnish, in a password-protected document or sealed cover, the Basic Subscriber Information and other relevant information … including name, address, contact details, e-mail addresses, bank details, IP logs and allied records” within “one week of receipt of the Notification,” and notifies “all uploaders, news portals, bloggers, account holders and other concerned persons” to take down and be restrained from re‑posting or disseminating the concerned content; Annexure‑I lists eight specific URLs (URLs 1–8).
0660fc344a.so_what: As stated in the Notification, intermediaries (including social media intermediaries, search engines, web‑hosting platforms, digital media platforms, internet service providers and other online service providers) and the listed publishers/users must remove/de-index the specified content/URLs within 24 hours of receipt and preserve and furnish the named subscriber/account information in a password‑protected document or sealed cover within one week of receipt.

3e7ac182a1.brief: This NCCS notice (published 16-06-2026) opens a stakeholder consultation by publishing the "Draft Generic Test Cases (along with expected result for PASS) for Charging Function (CHF) of 5G" on the NCCS website (https://nccs.gov.in/public/circulars_sas/test_cases_CHF.pdf). The notice invokes the Central Government's exercise of powers under Section 7 of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 and cites the amendment introducing Rules 528 to 537 in Part XI of the Indian Telegraph Rules, 1951 under the heading "Testing & Certification of Telegraph," which the notice states "mandate prior testing and certification for all telecommunication equipment," and it references the TEC "Procedure for Mandatory Testing and Certification of Telecommunication Equipment (MTCTE)" (Dec 2017) and the ITSAR for CHF of 5G published on 29-12-2023 (https://nccs.gov.in/public/itsar/ITSAR111172312.pdf). The notice states the stakeholder consultation "will remain open for a period of 60 days from the date of publication" and that "All stakeholders are requested to submit their comments and feedback on the draft Test Cases, no later than 16-08-2026" to the email addresses adg2sasf.nccs-dot@gov.in and dirttsc3.bg-dot@nic.in; it also supplies contact names, emails and phone numbers for Mr. Manas Kumar Panda (ADG(SAS-II)) and Mr. Ashish Chugh (Director (SAS-II)).
3e7ac182a1.so_what: The document opens a 60-day stakeholder consultation from 16-06-2026 and requires submission of comments no later than 16-08-2026 to adg2sasf.nccs-dot@gov.in and dirttsc3.bg-dot@nic.in, per the notice.

e5adb806a5.brief: This document is the Draft Telecommunications (Television, Radio and Associated Services) Rules, 2026 published by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (dated 12th June 2026) for public and inter‑ministerial consultation; the draft states it consolidates prior guidelines (listed at a)-f) with their dates) into a unified rule‑book and is made “in exercise of the powers conferred by” the specified sub‑sections of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 (quoted in the preamble). Rule 1(1) gives the short title and rule 1(2) provides that “They shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may specify by notification.” The draft publishes a consultation process: it was placed on www.mib.gov.in and invites “Inputs, comments, or suggestions” to the Under Secretary (BP&L), Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, New Delhi, “preferably, by email at usbpl‑moib@gov.in, by the 27th July, 2026.” Rule 2 contains definitions including (inter alia) “Act” means the Telecommunications Act, 2023 (rule 2(1)); “community radio service” is defined as “broadcasting of audio messages in a linear manner using radio waves to serve a local community within a specified geographical area with transmission range not exceeding ten kilometers from the specified geo‑coordinates” (rule 2(6)); “DSNG” is defined (rule 2(7)); “internet protocol television service” is defined (rule 2(8)); and other definitions appear at rules 2(2)–2(14) (the extracted text truncates within definition 2(14)).
e5adb806a5.so_what: The draft states it will be brought into force by a subsequent notification (rule 1(2)) and sets definitional thresholds that would apply if notified, for example defining “community radio service” with a transmission range “not exceeding ten kilometers from the specified geo‑coordinates” (rule 2(6)); the draft was open for comments until 27 July 2026 to usbpl‑moib@gov.in.

e95ed4a32e.brief: This Direction (No. 12-37/2017-B&CS) is issued by TRAI, dated 3 December, 2018, under "section 13, read with sub-clause (ii) of clause (b) of sub section (1) of section 11, of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997". It directs "all broadcasters and distributors of the television channels" "to restrain from placing any registered satellite television channel, whose TV rating is released by TV rating agency, on the landing LCN or landing channel or the boot-up screen with immediate effect." For "previously entered agreements, efforts may be made to implement these directions as soon as possible and it shall be implemented in all cases by 31st March 2019." The Direction also requires that "the information of such pre-existing agreements with full details of the parties to the agreement, the territory, agreement period and other relevant details may be submitted to the authority within seven days from the date of issuance of this direction at email:advbcs-2@trai.gov.in."
e95ed4a32e.so_what: Broadcasters and distributors covered by the Direction must not place any registered satellite television channel (whose TV rating is released by a TV rating agency) on the landing LCN/landing channel/boot-up screen immediately, must implement this in all cases by 31 March 2019 for pre-existing agreements, and must submit full details of any pre-existing agreements to advbcs-2@trai.gov.in within seven days of the Direction's date.

e452827779.brief: The document presented is titled "Cyber Security Guidelines for Smart City Infrastructure" and is described in the text as "a joint initiative of Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) and M/s Kaspersky." It states its purpose as to "establish a foundational digitally resilient framework for protecting Smart City digital infrastructure" and to "outline[] good practices and architectural strategies for safeguarding Smart City systems by the State/Union Territory (UT) Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT) and Smart City operators." The supplied pages include table of contents and sections such as "1. Introduction", "1.1. Key Smart City Infrastructure components", "1.2. Target Audience" and "2. Threat Landscape for Smart Cities" and expressly states "The audience for this document includes urban infrastructure managers, policy makers, Smart City technology providers and cybersecurity professionals." The supplied text also mentions the Smart Cities Mission launch date as "25 June, 2015" but does not include an issuance date for this instrument nor any explicit mandatory obligations, thresholds, or compliance deadlines in the provided pages.
e452827779.so_what: On the face of the supplied text, the concrete effect is that the guideline's contents (good practices and architectural strategies) are directed to State/UT CSIRTs and Smart City operators and the listed target audience ("urban infrastructure managers, policy makers, Smart City technology providers and cybersecurity professionals").

9db25c3920.brief: This document is CERT-In's "Technical Guidelines on SBOM, QBOM & CBOM, AIBOM and HBOM Version 2.0" (Version 2.0 Dated 09.07.2025). At Executive Summary and section 2.1 it states that "Departments and organizations are encouraged to make the creation and provision of Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) a mandatory standard practice as part of software procurement and software development" and that SBOMs should be used to "improve security, compliance, risk management, supply chain transparency, quality assurance, interoperability, and vendor management". Section 2.2 (Application & Scope) specifies the guideline has been issued by CERT-In "for the following entities especially in the Government, Public Sector, Essential Services Organizations and organizations involved with software exports and software services industry" and lists i. "Software Consumer", ii. "Software Developer" and iii. "System Integrator/Software Reseller". The document further "recommend[s] that all the Government, Public Sector and Essential Services Organizations should include requirements for SBOM in all their software and solutions purchase/procurement" and that "security teams of user organizations should include SBOM inventory in work flow of vulnerability management."
9db25c3920.so_what: The text directs that, as of Version 2.0 dated 09.07.2025, CERT-In expects SBOM creation/provision to be encouraged as a mandatory standard practice in software procurement and development for the listed entities (Government, Public Sector, Essential Services, software exporters/services), and it recommends inclusion of SBOM inventory in vulnerability-management workflows.

5f881c9da2.brief: This instrument is titled "Blueprint for Reducing Exposure and Defending against AI-Assisted Vulnerabilities Exploitation in Digital Infrastructure", issued by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) as Version 1.0 dated 25.05.2026. It provides an implementation-oriented framework (see Table of Contents and Executive Summary) that "covers: i. Governance and accountability mechanisms. ii. Exposure reduction strategies. iii. Technical defensive controls. iv. AI-aware security operations. v. Vulnerability and exposure management. vi. Supply-chain security. vii. Incident response and cyber resilience. viii. Continuous security validation. ix. Workforce preparedness and operational readiness." The text uses recommendatory and prescriptive wording for organisations: the Executive Summary states "Organisations are encouraged to implement the recommendations contained in this blueprint in a risk -informed manner" and Section 5 states "Organisations should adopt AI enabled adaptive, intelligence-driven, continuously validated, and resilience-oriented cybersecurity practices"; the blueprint explicitly identifies applicability to "vital sectors including government, finance, telecommunications, Digital Public Infrastructure, healthcare, energy, transportation, manufacturing, and digital services" (Section 4.5).
5f881c9da2.so_what: As drafted, the document (Version 1.0 | 25.05.2026) communicates that "Organisations are encouraged to implement the recommendations contained in this blueprint in a risk -informed manner" (Executive Summary) and that "Organisations should adopt AI enabled adaptive, intelligence-driven, continuously validated, and resilience-oriented cybersecurity practices" (Section 5), and it names specific vital sectors to which the threat analysis and recommendations apply (Section 4.5).

5b465de1d6.brief: CERT-In’s document titled "Cyber Security Framework and Guidelines for Space including Satellite Communication" is a CERT-In direction (instrument text provided has no date) that sets out a comprehensive, risk-based framework and segment-wise security controls for SatCom systems (see Table of Contents and Executive Summary). It identifies covered stakeholders by name: "government agencies, satellite service providers, ground station operators, terminal equipment vendors, and private space entities" (Executive Summary, Introduction) and states it "establish[es] minimum security requirements, recommended best practices, and governance mechanisms" for those entities (Introduction). The instrument contains a specific operative obligation in Section 3.2.1 "Incident Reporting and Response": "All SatCom operators and service providers must report cybersecurity incidents, breaches, or anomalies within 6 hours of noticing the incident to CERT-In. Detailed information can be found at www.cert-in.org.in." The document also references appointment of a "Chief Satellite Security Officer (CSSO)/ Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)" (Definitions, 2.1.1), segment-wise controls (Executive Summary; Section 6 title in TOC), and Annexure C: "CERT-In’s Incident Reporting Format."
5b465de1d6.so_what: Per Section 3.2.1, the text requires that "All SatCom operators and service providers must report cybersecurity incidents, breaches, or anomalies within 6 hours of noticing the incident to CERT-In."

43d4b28e9f.brief: This CERT-In document titled "15 Elemental Cyber Defense Controls for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)", Version 1.0 dated 01.09.2025, issues a 15-control cybersecurity baseline applicable to "Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) which are covered as per the criteria... notified... vide notification no. 2020 S.O. 1702(E) dated 1st June 2020". It lists 45 security baseline recommendations mapped to 15 Elemental Cyber Defense Controls (EAM, NES, EMS, SC, PM, IM, LM, AT, TPRM, DPBP, GC, RPP, ACIM, PS, VAA) and sets specific operational requirements and thresholds in individual identifiers (examples: IM.3 requires adherence to Directions under sub-section (6) of section 70B of the Information Technology Act, 2000 and states "Including Report cybersecurity incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of detection or notification"; LM.1 requires logs to be retained "for a minimum of 180 days with secure storage within Indian jurisdiction"; AT.1 requires basic cybersecurity awareness training "at least twice a year"; VAA.1 requires independent third-party vulnerability assessments "at least once a year"; ACIM.3 requires review/update of user access "periodically at least quarterly or immediately upon role changes"; RPP.1 prescribes passwords of "a minimum of 8 to 12 characters" and RPP.2 prescribes temporary account lock after "3 to 5 failed login attempts").
43d4b28e9f.so_what: Under IM.3 MSMEs must "adhere to Directions under sub-section (6) of section 70B of the Information Technology Act, 2000" and "Report cybersecurity incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of detection or notification" (as stated in the instrument).
